mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances following a FEDFUNDS increase > 0.25%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) indicates strengthening consumer demand, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances following a 3-month RSAFS increase.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month signals labor market weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate economic slowdown.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances following a UNRATE increase > 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% within a month signals supply-side weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to decline.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances following a INDPRO decrease > 1%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% within a month signals strengthening demand in the housing sector, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as related industries benefit.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances following a HOUST increase > 5%.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 jobs in a month, it signals a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and corporate earnings are expected to rise.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances following a PAYEMS increase > 200,000.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals inflationary pressure and tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances following the joint trigger condition.

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP (GDPC1) growth is negative for two consecutive quarters and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is above 7%, it signals a recessionary environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to decline.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 negative for 2 consecutive quarters and UNRATE > 7%
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances following the joint trigger condition.
